## Changed surface
6 production files: src/android/androidComposeTypes.ts (new), src/android/buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject.ts (new), src/android/index.ts (modified, barrel exports), src/indexing/managedArtifacts.ts (modified, new filename constant), src/indexing/writeIndexManifest.ts (modified, new optional write parameter), src/indexing/runIndexCommand.ts (modified, new builder call + analyzer-status function + wiring). Confirmed via graph-diff between the implementation and test indexes: additive-only symbol/edge growth, no unexpected file changed or removed.

## Production owners
src/android/ owns the new artifact type contract and analyzer (androidComposeTypes.ts, buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject.ts, index.ts barrel). src/indexing/ owns orchestration/registration/writing (managedArtifacts.ts, writeIndexManifest.ts, runIndexCommand.ts's finishIndexBuild()). Same ownership confirmed across architecture-context-packet.txt, implementation-context-packet.txt, and this stage's retrieval report.

## Production contracts
AndroidComposeSemanticArtifact / ComposeDeclarationEntry / ComposeChildCallEvidence / ComposeStructuralRegionEvidence / ComposeSemanticSummary (androidComposeTypes.ts) — see docs/GRAPH_SCHEMA.md's new "android-compose-semantic.json (v1.11.0 Batch 1)" section for the full field-level contract. buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject(options): BuildAndroidComposeSemanticProjectResult — the sole production entry point tests call directly (mirroring composeNavigationRoutes.spec.ts's pattern of calling the analyzer function directly rather than only through the CLI).

## Validators
No new shared validator module. Conservative parsing validators (annotation/function-pattern matching, brace/paren/string-literal handling) are internal to buildAndroidComposeSemanticProject.ts and are exercised indirectly through its public output, not unit-tested in isolation — consistent with how buildComposeNavigationRoutes.ts's internal helpers are tested only through its public `routes`/`screenCandidates`/`warnings` output in composeNavigationRoutes.spec.ts.

## Constants
ANDROID_COMPOSE_SEMANTIC_ARTIFACT_KIND = 'my-dev-kit-v1-android-compose-semantic', ANDROID_COMPOSE_SEMANTIC_SCHEMA_VERSION = '1.0.0', ANDROID_COMPOSE_SEMANTIC_FILENAME = 'android-compose-semantic.json' (androidComposeTypes.ts, re-exported from android/index.ts and consumed by managedArtifacts.ts/writeIndexManifest.ts/runIndexCommand.ts).

## Errors
No new thrown-error type. Per-file I/O errors are swallowed internally (file skipped, no warning). A genuine internal exception during the builder's own construction is caught at the finishIndexBuild() call site (runAndroidComposeSemanticAnalyzer's try/catch) and reported as analyzer status 'failed' with errorCount:1 — mirrors the classification/android-components failure-mode contract exactly; not independently tested with a forced-throw fixture in this batch (no existing sibling analyzer test does this either).

## Unresolved items
None blocking. Three low-likelihood conservative-scanner edge cases are documented as accepted risks in implementation-report.txt ("Unresolved risks"): multi-line triple-quoted strings, `<`/`>` used as comparison operators in default-parameter expressions, and local classes as an untracked nesting boundary. None are covered by a dedicated fixture in this batch; each is a narrow, low-real-world-likelihood gap consistent with the base Kotlin adapter's own documented conservative-parser limitations, not a defect requiring NEEDS_CORRECTION.

## Override authorization: CONTEXT_SUFFICIENT_BY_TARGETED_VERIFICATION_WITH_AUTOMATED_ROLE_ADEQUACY_FALSE_NEGATIVE (second instance, test-implementation stage)

After supplying all 32 TST-NNN IDs as testResponsibilityRefs, the raw capsule's responsibilityMappings evidence group applies a fixed limit of 25 mapping entries (responsibilityMappings.limit: 25, availableCount: 32, usedCount: 25, truncated: true, droppedCount: 7 — TST-026 through TST-032 dropped in deterministic order). This is the same category of fixed-per-group-budget false negative already documented and user-authorized for the implementation-context stage (see implementation-context-packet.txt's "## Override authorization" section) — a hard-coded evidence-group cap that is smaller than this batch's actual (larger than typical) responsibility count, not a sign that the 7 dropped responsibilities are actually unmapped or untested.
All 32 responsibilities, including the 7 dropped from the raw capsule's bounded mapping list (TST-026..TST-032), are independently confirmed mapped to passing tests in this same packet's "## Test responsibilities" section above, cross-checked directly against the actual test files and their pass/fail results (composeSemanticDeclarations.spec.ts: 20/20 passing; androidComposeSemanticIncremental.spec.ts: 10/10 passing; regression suites: 708/708 and 1908/1908 passing; static-analysis commands: all exit 0) — not against the capsule's own truncated summary.
Per the user's prior authorization (recorded verbatim in this run's history and referenced in implementation-context-packet.txt), this exception is treated as extending to this second, structurally identical instance of the same fixed-evidence-budget pattern: "The automated inadequacy result alone must not cause the implementation, judge, or final verdict to fail after this authorization... The final report must preserve the limitation and recommend a separate correction to the context-adequacy budgeting logic and the stage-context workflow gate." This is exactly that limitation, encountered a second time in the same run, and is called out explicitly in the final report as additional evidence supporting that recommended correction (the responsibility-mapping budget should scale with the actual number of requested testResponsibilityRefs, or the truncation should not automatically block when independently-verified evidence already exists).
No production code, test code, or my-dev-kit/my-dev-kit-orchestrator source was modified to obtain this override.

## Notes
Two context-gate overrides were required in this run (implementation-context and this test-context stage), both traced to the same class of fixed-evidence-group-budget tool limitation, both explicitly authorized and documented rather than silently bypassed.
